title: A protocol for identifying actin Lysine 84 monomethylation
protocol: Have nitrocellulose membrane ready, draw grid by pencil to indicate the region you are going to blot.
Spot 2 μl of samples onto the nitrocellulose membrane at the center of the grid using a narrow-mouth pipet tip.
Let the membrane dry.
Transfer the membrane to 5 ml Ponceau S Stain solution.
Place the membrane on an orbital shaker for 15 min at room temperature.
Rinse membrane with ddH2O to achieve desired staining; approximately 1-2 washes of 2 min each will remove background staining.
Record the result by camera.
Wash the membrane 2-3 times with ddH2O for 5 min each to remove Ponceau S.
Block non-specific sites by soaking in 5% Non-Fat milk in TBS-T for 0.5 h at RT.
Incubate with primary antibody dissolved in 5% Non-Fat milk in TBS-T for 2 h at RT.
Wash three times with TBS-T (3 × 5 min).
Incubate with secondary antibody conjugated with HRP for 30 min at RT.
Wash three times with TBS-T (3 × 5 min), then once with TBS (5 min).
Incubate with ECL reagent for 5 min and expose X-ray film in the dark room.
Compare the signal from your unknown sample to that of standard and estimate the concentration.
Prepare the cell lysate using ice cold 0.1% NET Buffer.
Mix EZview Red Anti-HA Affinity Gel beads until completely and uniformly suspended.
Add 100 µl of the 50% slurry into a clean 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Wash beads twice in 0.1% NET Buffer by adding 750 µl of NET 0.1% Buffer to the tube.
Centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for approximately 30 s at 6,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Generate whole cell extract by lysing cells in 0.1% NET buffer followed by sonication using a Sonic Dismembrator (10% output, 1 min, with 10 s-on and 20 s-off cycles).
Centrifuge the lysate for 10 min at 14,000 × g in a microcentrifuge at 4°C.
Carefully remove the clear lysate supernatant with a 1 ml micropipette and transfer into the tube of equilibrated EZview Red Anti-HA Affinity Gel beads.
Incubate with thorough, gentle mixing for 3 h at 4°C.
Centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for 30 s at 6,000 × g.
Aspirate supernatant carefully.
Wash the bead pellet by adding 1 ml of TBS.
Incubate with thorough, gentle mixing at 4°C for 5 min.
Centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for 30 s at 6,000 × g.
Aspirate supernatant carefully and set the tube with the bead pellet on ice.
Repeat washes two more times as described previously.
Elute the HA-fusion protein with HA peptide by adding the desired volume of a freshly prepared 100 µg/ml solution in 50 mM pH 7.4 Tris-HCl buffer.
Incubate the affinity gel sample for 10 min and recover the supernatant after pelleting the affinity gel by centrifugation.
Add 4 fold volume of –20°C acetone to ice-cold sample solution.
Mix well and keep at –20°C for at least 30 min.
Spin in a refrigerated microfuge at top speed for 30 min.
Remove supernatant and air-dry the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 8 M urea, 100 mM Tris, pH 8.5 for 0.5 ml urea buffer by mixing 240 mg urea, 100 μl 500 mM Tris pH8.5, and 220 μl H₂O.
Sonicate the resuspended pellet for 10 min.
Add TCEP to a final concentration of 5 mM and incubate at RT for 20 min.
Add iodoacetamide to 10 mM and incubate at RT for 15 min in the dark.
Dilute to 2 M urea with 100 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.5.
Add methylamine to 20 mM to reduce carbamylation.
Add Asp-N according to a ratio of 1:50 enzyme : substrate and incubate overnight at 37 ºC in the dark.
Add EDTA to 0.5 mM to inactivate Asp-N.
Add DTT to 5 mM, CaCl₂ to 8.5 mM and Arg-C according to a ratio of 1:50 enzyme : substrate, and incubate for 8 hours at 37 ºC in the dark.
Quench with 5% Formic acid.
Load samples onto a precolumn (250 μm ID) with 2 cm C18 resin (10 μm) under flow rate of about 1 μl/min.
Wash with 0.1% Formic acid for 10 min.
Elute with 20 μl 80% ACN, 0.1% Formic acid.
Dry with Centrivap.
Resuspend with the NET buffer (without NP-40).
Take 20 μl of protein A beads slurry for one sample and spin at 6,000 for 1 min, at 4ºC.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash beads twice in NET Buffer (without NP-40) by adding 750 µl of NET Buffer to the tube and centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for approximately 30 s at 6,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Add peptides to the beads.
Add proper NET buffer to the tube up to 500 µl.
Incubate in a 4°C rotator for 60 minutes.
Spin at 10,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2 µg of purified Rabbit IgG control antibody or 2 µg anti-K84me1 antibody to the pre-cleaned cell lysate.
Incubate in a 4°C rotator for 2 hours.
Wash 40 µl of protein A beads three times with NET buffer (without NP-40).
Add the lysate and antibody mixture to the washed beads.
Incubate in a 4°C rotator for 1 hour at 4°C with gentle agitation.
Spin in centrifuge at 6,000 × g at 4°C for 1 minute.
Discard supernatant.
Wash the beads five times with 1 × TBS buffer (add 1 mM PMSF before use).
Agitate the tube in a 4°C rotator for 5 minutes each time.
Spin down the beads at 6,000 × g at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Remove the supernatant carefully and completely.
Add 70 µl elution buffer (0.1 M glycine, pH 2.5) to each sample and control resin.
Incubate with gentle shaking for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Do not leave the resin in this buffer more than 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the resin for 1 minute at 8,200 × g.
Transfer the supernatants to fresh test tubes containing 7 µl 1 M Tris HCl, pH 8.0.
Be careful not to transfer any resin.
Load samples onto a precolumn with 2 cm C18 resin under a flow rate of about 1 μl/min.
Wash with 0.1% formic acid for 10 min.
Elute with 20 μl of 80% ACN and 0.1% formic acid.
Dry the eluted samples using Centrivap.
Resuspend dried samples in 0.1% formic acid.
Set up the pre-column with 100 μm ID, packed with 6 cm C18 resin (10 μm).
Set up the analytical column with a 75 μm ID pulled tip less than 5 μm and packed with 12 cm C18 resin (3 μm).
Equilibrate the pre-column with 10 μl of buffer A (0.1% formic acid) under pressure of 280 Bar.
Equilibrate the analytical column with 3 μl of buffer A under pressure of 280 Bar.
Pick 5 μl sample and load it onto the column using 12 μl total volume (including additional 7 μl of buffer A) at a flow rate of 2 μl/min or pressure of 280 Bar.
Initiate gradient elution from time 0 to 5 minutes with buffer B mixture of 3%.
Continue gradient elution from time 5 to 65 minutes with buffer B mixture increasing linearly to 25%.
Proceed with a steep gradient increase in buffer B mixture from time 65 to 74 minutes up to 80%.
Maintain buffer B at 80% for the remaining time.
For peptide identification, search MS2 spectra against an EPI-IPI human database.
Consider carbamidomethylation on Cysteine as a fixed modification.
Treat mono-, di- or tri-methylation at Lys as differential modifications.
Filter search results using DTASelect 2.0 with 10 p.p.m. mass accuracy for precursor mass.
Apply a 1% FDR cutoff at the spectral level.
Annotate b-actin K84me1 spectra using pLabel, requiring 20 p.p.m. accuracy for fragment ions.
